points: Measured latency is dominated by geometry_core::estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, called from PalletPoseNode::on_pair once per admitted detection (max_stage2 defaults to 2, serial, one shared rng). two_stage_chamfer_search_v2 always runs. two_stage_chamfer_search_v2_with_prior also runs unless the free chamfer cost is already at or below about 0.00623 m, the point where lambda_eff = prior_lambda 3.0 * (1 - confidence) reaches lambda_floor 0.05. Default grids: free coarse 21 theta x 31 x 31 = 20181 (±10 deg at 1 deg, ±0.15 m at 0.01 m), free fine 13 x 25 x 25 = 8125 (±1.2 deg at 0.2 deg, ±0.012 m at 0.001 m), prior coarse 21 x 21 x 21 = 9261 (±0.10 m at 0.01 m, same ±10 deg), prior fine another 8125, so about 45692 chamfer_cost_from_rotated evaluations on the common path, plus a few full chamfer_cost_v2 calls (pi-ambiguity pair, each stage's init pose, anchor cost, and a second data-only cost after the prior search discards prior_search_cost). OpenMP schedule(static) splits the flattened (theta, y, x) index and does not reduce that count.

Published PoseResult does not use the chamfer argmin, but the search is still paid on every successful inference. tx/ty/tz are the bbox-centre ray_plane_intersect_cross_camera hit mapped by R_dr/t_dr, and yaw_rad is yaw_from_normal_camera of the plane normal. best_pose.theta_rad and the search cost are stored only on ChamferDebugV3_2. The admitted extents are a separate pass on that same estimate: after the search, one O(n_inliers) loop over plane_points_3d sets width_m to the camera-x span, height_m to the camera-y span, and depth_m to the mean range, and sets has_dimensions only when that inlier face is non-empty. That loop is negligible beside the chamfer grid. It is the measurement /pps/pallet_pose_rich must carry with this pose, and only when the estimate produced the inliers.

Each chamfer hypothesis is O(N log N) with a full copy. The cached prototype has N=182 contour samples (outer 1.20 x 0.14 m plus two 0.47 x 0.10 m pockets at contour_spacing_m 0.03). rotate_proto_into (out = proto * R.transpose()) is cached once per theta in thread-local ChamferTls, but chamfer_cost_from_rotated still assigns tls.translated = rotated (N x 2 doubles) and adds tx and ty on every (x, y) candidate. sample_bilinear_into indexes that column-major MatrixXd as (i, 0) and (i, 1) and bilinear-samples all 182 points from the float distance image (four taps promoted to double). trimmed_mean_from_distances copies all N distances into a std::vector and std::sorts them, then sums the shortest ceil(0.9*N)=164 for trim_fraction 0.10. Cost is O(T * N log N) with T about 45692, not a partial select of the kept prefix. The prototype cache and ChamferTls avoid rebuilding the contour and per-candidate heap growth; those buffers are still recopied and sorted on every grid cell.

The distance image sampled by that search is built once per detection on a padding-dominated grid. rasterize_points_to_mask uses resolution_m 0.005 and padding_m 0.80 (160 px on each side), so a 1.20 x 0.14 m face becomes about 560 x 350 cells (~2e5 pixels). close_mask clones that mask, runs an elliptical MORPH_CLOSE, connectedComponentsWithStats, and writes a second full image. compute_distance_transform_v2 compare-builds an 8-bit source, calls cv::distanceTransform with DIST_L2 and DIST_MASK_PRECISE, and convertTo-copies the result to CV_32FC1. That precise OpenCV distance transform is the main one-shot image cost; every later hypothesis random-accesses the float image. OpenCV imgproc is the heavy one-shot dependency.

sample_face_points scans the entire depth frame per admitted detection, not the bbox, and that cloud is what the inlier-face extents are measured on. camera.yaml is 640 x 480 depth and 1920 x 1080 RGB, so each detection does 307200 per-pixel K_inv multiplies, SE3 transforms into the RGB camera, pinhole projections, and a lookup in a full RGB-sized mask, with cv::Mat::at bounds checks. Accepted points are push_back'd into per-thread std::vector<Eigen::Vector3d> buckets and copied row-by-row into a column-major Eigen::MatrixXd. build_bbox_mask allocates and erodes a full 1920 x 1080 mask (erode_px 2) for a single rectangle. depth_image_to_meters convertTo-copies the whole depth image to CV_32FC1 once per synced pair, before that scan repeats for each admitted box.

Plane fitting materializes the inlier cloud the extents loop reads, and it allocates on every RANSAC trial. ransac_plane_fit (ransac_iters 100, early stop at inlier ratio 0.85) builds a new residual ArrayXd and bool mask every iteration, copies inliers into a fresh MatrixXd, and JacobiSVD-refits. estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 then calls plane_inlier_mask again and copies those inliers into plane_points_3d, the matrix whose camera-x span, camera-y span, and mean range become width_m, height_m, and depth_m. project_points_to_plane_2d allocates a full relative-point matrix plus the 2D result, and estimate_pca_long_axis allocates another centred copy of every 2D inlier. These Eigen copies are O(N) and smaller than the chamfer grid, and they run again for the second admitted detection. A change to this inlier copy changes both latency and the extents published with the pose.

Stage-1 detection sits on the measured path before any stage-2 work. RtDetrDetector.detect copies the ROS buffer via bytes(msg.data) into a contiguous RGB array (channel reverse for bgr8; mono8 repeats the gray plane three times), then preprocess cv2.resize to 640x640 with INTER_LINEAR (no letterbox), astype float32, transpose to CHW, divide by 255, and ascontiguousarray a (1, 3, 640, 640) batch. Postprocess is a score filter and argsort of the engine's top-k, not NMS. The default node backend is mock. When the backend is TensorRT, TensorRTBackend.infer also copies images and orig_target_sizes into pagelocked host buffers, memcpy_htod_async, execute_async_v3 or execute_async_v2, synchronizes, and copies labels, boxes, and scores back. The pose node runs only after message_filters sync of that detection array with depth.
